    - needs something a later task introduces;
    - contradicts another step;
    - cannot run as written;
    - needs authority you do not have;
    - has a test or example that would not give the result the plan claims.
  Name the step and what you found in the report. Stopping then is the correct outcome, not a failure. Do not improvise.

  When you finish, write a report (under 20 lines: whether the task is complete, anything you changed that the brief did not ask for, anything you could
  not verify) and hand it back. Write the report to a file with your file-write tool, never through cat or a heredoc. Then run this in the foreground,
  never in the background, and wait for it to return:

      tandem-handback --root '/tmp/greet' --task 2 --run
  0a72e3f813ae13311e6cae5c9e9b6601 --attempt 3251db3485881d2c01bceeee0e56fb1c --job 95fc41a7a6cd0c92d77cac1789dfde92 --effect
  7b5e5e3d0bb9923be4ec739ebf2c448c --nonce 6c6029c417481591cd91d82a49f486d6 --report <file>

  Add --stuck if you could not finish. That call returns immediately. Then stop.
